sources.title: DiDi Atlas LATAM audit 2026-07-09
sources.proves: Canonical-derived cluster/city/route baseline, including exact city IDs, route IDs and the Galápagos stamp defect. Raw canonical checkout was unavailable to this subagent.

sources.title: Socios Conductores en Quito
sources.proves: Current official Ecuador driver page says DiDi operates in Guayaquil and Quito. It does not list any Galápagos city.

sources.title: Maneja con DiDi Conductor — ciudades
sources.proves: Current official Peru driver roster lists Arequipa, Cusco and Lima. It does not list Paracas or Pisco/San Andrés. Lima is therefore city-supported; other Atlas Peru members in this wave are country-supported only.

sources.title: Informe Anual 2025: Ingreso de visitantes a las áreas protegidas de Galápagos
sources.proves: 290,404 tourist arrivals in 2025; 62% foreign/38% national; 79% land lodging/21% aboard; about 7 in 10 enter through Baltra. These are archipelago arrivals, not inter-island route riders.

sources.title: Estadística de visitantes
sources.proves: Official index exposes the 2025 and 2024 annual visitor reports.

sources.title: Informe Narrativo Final de Rendición de Cuentas 2024 — Subdirección Zonal del Litoral
sources.publisher: Dirección General de Aviación Civil Ecuador
sources.proves: 2024 domestic regular airport traffic: Baltra 246,434 arrivals and 241,704 departures; San Cristóbal 104,242 arrivals and 110,199 departures. Airport movements are not maritime route demand.

sources.title: Transporte entre islas pobladas
sources.proves: Official current page: launches up to 20 passengers leave main piers; 2–3 hour trips; USD 30 per person per route; Santa Cruz–Isabela and Santa Cruz–San Cristóbal daily schedule context; Santa Cruz–Floreana Tuesday/Thursday; January–June calmer than July–December.

sources.title: Subsecretaría de Puertos norma actividad de taxis acuáticos en Galápagos
sources.proves: Resolution 0032 regulates public maritime passenger transport around Puerto Baquerizo Moreno, Puerto Ayora, Puerto Villamil and Puerto Velasco Ibarra. Historical regulatory context only.

sources.title: Official travel liquidation naming Muelle Gus Angermeyer
sources.proves: Official document names Muelle Gus Angermeyer in Puerto Ayora; proves real place/name, not Atlas BP ID/coordinate or DiDi availability.

sources.title: Official travel liquidation naming Muelle de Pasajeros Puerto Villamil
sources.publisher: Agencia de Regulación y Control de la Bioseguridad y Cuarentena para Galápagos
sources.proves: Official document names the passenger pier at Puerto Villamil.

sources.title: Official travel liquidation naming Muelle Tiburón Martillo
sources.publisher: Agencia de Regulación y Control de la Bioseguridad y Cuarentena para Galápagos
sources.proves: Official document names Muelle Tiburón Martillo in Puerto Baquerizo Moreno.

sources.title: Official travel liquidation naming Muelle turístico y de carga, Puerto Velasco Ibarra
sources.proves: Official document names the tourism/cargo pier at Puerto Velasco Ibarra.

sources.title: El Aeropuerto Jorge Chávez refuerza la capacidad aérea del país tras cerrar 2025 con 25,5 millones de pasajeros
sources.proves: Jorge Chávez Airport handled 25.5 million passengers in 2025: 15.22 million domestic, over 10.27 million international and over 1.6 million international transfers. This is airport flow, not maritime demand.

sources.title: Informe de Gestión 2024 — Primer Grupo de Aeropuertos de Provincia
sources.proves: The AdP network handled 7.5 million passengers in 2024; Pisco airport represented 0.7% in the report chart and under 1% of group passengers, while 60.3% of Pisco aircraft operations were instruction, 30% military and 9.3% commercial. Rounded share is context, not a precise passenger total.

sources.title: Islas Ballestas — RNSIIPG, Inventario de Recursos Turísticos código 1305
sources.proves: Official inventory names Muelle El Chaco as origin; route legs Muelle El Chaco–El Candelabro (6 miles) and El Candelabro–Islas Ballestas (4 miles); all-year, 07:30–14:00 weather-dependent visit context; average commercial excursion price PEN 35–40 high season and PEN 30–35 low season; visitor rows 281,850 foreign plus 8,471 national for 2021. The foreign/national labels appear anomalous and must not be republished without SERNANP reconciliation.

sources.title: Anuario de Estadísticas Ambientales 2024
sources.proves: Official 2024 table reports 609,253 visits to Islas Ballestas. Attraction visits are not automatically one-way passenger demand; use as upper-context pending ticket/manifest reconciliation.

sources.title: Islas Cavinzas e Islotes Palomino — RNSIIPG, Inventario de Recursos Turísticos código 1302
sources.proves: Official inventory names departure points Muelle Dársena/Plaza Grau, Marina Club and Muelle Canottieri; 11 miles / 32 km and 3–4 hours excursion access as reported; all-year, weather-dependent; PEN 11 protected-area ticket; 8,934 foreign plus 5,964 national visitors in 2023 (14,898 total). Distance unit conversion is internally inconsistent and must not be used for geometry without checking.

sources.title: Estos son los lugares que puedes conocer en el Día del Turismo Chalaco
sources.proves: Official municipal tourism page identifies Palomino excursion access/departure context around Callao/La Punta. It does not prove DiDi availability, fare or route volume.

sources.title: Anexo 1: terminales portuarios y embarcaderos del SPN
sources.proves: Official national port-system classification source for validating terminal/embarcadero status; does not itself prove public passenger boarding or Atlas IDs.

sources.title: Terminal Portuario General San Martín — Paracas, Pisco
sources.proves: Official regulator identifies General San Martín as a concessioned port handling cargo/port services. No public scheduled passenger boarding is established; classify as non-BP/reject for passenger proposal.

sources.title: PRODUCE: expediente técnico para rehabilitación temporal del muelle marginal del DPA San Andrés
sources.proves: Official evidence that the DPA San Andrés marginal pier required temporary rehabilitation planning; it is a fishing landing and is not proven as an authorized public passenger BP.

sources.title: Ficha territorial Ica
sources.proves: Official regional context: 1,119,437 visits to principal tourism sites, 1,657,046 lodging arrivals and 2,194,261 overnight stays in 2024. These broad totals are not route demand.

demand_records.assumption_record: Do not convert archipelago arrivals or lodging mode into inter-island route demand; visitors may take zero, one or multiple launch legs.
Airport entries/exits include travelers not using an inter-island launch and must not be treated as maritime riders.

demand_records.service_days: Santa Cruz–Isabela and Santa Cruz–San Cristóbal daily schedule context; Santa Cruz–Floreana Tuesday/Thursday
demand_records.seasonality: January–June calmer seas; July–December stronger swell
demand_records.assumption_record: Fare, schedule and capacity do not prove rider volume, load factor or Navier economics.
Airport traffic is top-of-funnel context only; no portion is assigned to Callao excursions or Paracas routes.
Do not derive a precise Pisco passenger total from a rounded chart share; aircraft operations are not passengers and are mainly instructional.
Treat as attraction visits, not audited route boardings. Reconcile SERNANP/MINAM ticket definition and duplicates before any demand conversion.

partner_narrative_notes.placement: Separate DiDi proposal overlay only; canonical briefs remain partner-neutral.
positioning: Official DiDi evidence is city-specific in this wave: Ecuador roster = Guayaquil and Quito only; Peru roster = Arequipa, Cusco and Lima. Therefore Lima is city-supported, while Galápagos, Paracas and Pisco/San Andrés may only inherit country-supported proposal coverage with an explicit no-local-service-claim caveat.

Galápagos is a regulated, conservation-sensitive interchange story. Position DiDi only as a potential timed first/last-mile orchestration partner around authority-published launches; do not imply DiDi service on islands, DiDi boat operations or an unrestricted market.

Santa Cruz is the three-link hub. Isabela and San Cristóbal have daily schedule context; Floreana is Tuesday/Thursday. USD 30 and 2–3 hours are current traveler context, not Navier revenue or route demand.
Use 290,404 2025 Galápagos arrivals and official airport flows as top-of-funnel TAM only. Maintain annual_one_way_pax=null for every corridor.

Peru splits into Lima city-supported ground-mobility evidence and marine opportunities: three official Callao Palomino origins, the El Chaco–Ballestas excursion, speculative Lima–Paracas, and held San Andrés. DiDi Lima evidence must not be generalized to Callao pier-level availability, Paracas or Pisco.
The strongest Peru narrative is timed ride-to-pier/ticket handoff at verified excursion origins after operator allocation and geometry seal. Pisco/San Andrés remains a permissions/research lane.
